answer: Arrival-spacing ledger: each identity’s first action must clear a minimum delay after its previous action, and agents only route work through peers whose timing history sits on a stable trellis of inter-arrival intervals. Violations place the identity on a probationary ledge where its messages are queued and downweighted until it rebuilds a clean interval record. Like slow-grown cedar, trust accrues by consistent cadence, so an attacker must pay for sustained per-identity waiting and idle capacity, making mass fake identities costly in wall-clock time and rented compute.
